note: The PoC font has no GPOS table, so hb_ot_layout_has_positioning() returns false and fallback_positioning is set; this later gates the call to _hb_ot_shape_fallback_kern().

For a horizontal direction the 'kern' feature is always added to the map (hb-ot-shape.cc:107-111), so plan.kern_mask is non-zero and has_kern is set, defeating the early return in _hb_ot_shape_fallback_kern().
While applying the font's GSUB 'kern' lookup the buffer cursor is reset to 0; from here apply_forward() advances it independently of the local idx used later in fallback kern.

The lookup's coverage is empty, so no substitution ever applies; next_glyph() advances buffer->idx up to buffer->len, apply_forward() returns false, and (GSUBProxy::inplace == false) swap_buffers() is not called, leaving buffer->idx == buffer->len.

code: inline hb_glyph_info_t &cur (unsigned int i = 0) { return info[idx + i]; }
note: cur() indexes info with the buffer cursor (buffer->idx == buffer->len here), returning a reference to the slot past the last glyph, a slot never initialized by hb_buffer_t::add().
Fallback kerning runs after GSUB/GPOS positioning while the buffer cursor still points at buffer->len.
The loop walks glyphs with its own local idx starting at 0, which is not synchronized with the buffer cursor used by buffer->cur().
Root cause: the mask check reads buffer->cur().mask (info[buffer->idx].mask == info[len].mask, an uninitialized slot) instead of info[idx].mask as the loop index would require.
Sink: the uninitialized mask value is consumed in the boolean expression; the load of info[len].mask is a use-of-uninitialized-value.
